Check prerequisites against practice logs

Source: R/kt-prereq.R
mv_kt_prereq.Rd

Experimental. Asks the practice logs which concepts are learned faster once another concept is known. If A is a prerequisite of B, students who do not yet know A should learn B slowly, and pick it up quickly once A is known. For every ordered pair of skills, the learn rate of B is estimated twice from a knowledge tracing model (mv_kt_fit()): On the attempts made while A was probably known (its probability of being known, from the student's earlier attempts on A, is above 0.5) and on those made while it was not. A likelihood ratio test compares this with one learn rate.

Usage

mv_kt_prereq(kt, kg = NULL, alpha = 0.001, min_ratio = 2, min_share = 0.05)

Arguments

kt

a knowledge tracing model from mv_kt_fit(); its skills must be concepts of kg.

kg

the knowledge graph to check; by default the graph kt was fitted with.

alpha

significance level of the likelihood ratio tests.

min_ratio

smallest speed-up (learn rate with the prerequisite known divided by the rate without) that suggests a missing edge.

min_share

smallest share of the attempts in each group for a pair to be judged; pairs where nearly everyone (or no one) knows A cannot show a difference.

Value

An mv_kt_prereq object: A list with pairs (one row per ordered pair: from, to, edge, learn_without, learn_with, ratio, lr (the likelihood ratio statistic), p_value, share_with, n_attempts and verdict), flags, kg and settings. Use tidy(), glance() and print().

Details

Concepts on the same learning path all speed each other up, so each test is run on the attempts where B's other prerequisites in the graph are already known: An indirect prerequisite then adds little. A graph edge whose test fails is flagged weak_prerequisite; a pair without an edge whose test is clearly significant, with a large speed-up and enough attempts in both groups, is flagged missing_prerequisite. Of two concepts that speed each other up, only the stronger direction is suggested. Like mv_kg_fit(), the flags are leads for content experts, not verdicts; add or drop edges with mv_kg_edit() and check again.

See also

mv_kg_fit() checks the same graph against test answers.

Examples

kt <- mv_kt_fit(fractions_logs, kg = fractions_kg)
check <- mv_kt_prereq(kt)
check
#> <mv_kt_prereq> (EXPERIMENTAL) Prerequisites checked against practice logs
#> Graph: Grade 5 fractions; 5 prerequisite edge(s), 5 supported by the logs
#> 1 flag(s)
#> * [missing_prerequisite] compare is learned 10.1 times as fast once
#>   equivalent is known (learn 0.17 vs 0.02, LR = 155.6); add the
#>   prerequisite equivalent -> compare? 
tidy(check)
